senses.definition: Aware of something and visibly taking it into account, especially something you were expected to have noticed. It says the thing was in view when the decision was made, not merely that you know it now.
senses.caution: A memo word, not a spoken one. Said aloud it sounds stiff and aware would do the same job, but in writing it earns its place because it puts on record that you knew and weighed something, which is exactly what an auditor or a regulator is reading for. Be careful claiming it after the fact about a risk you plainly missed, and note that a large IT services firm carries the name, so in a vendor conversation there will be a beat where someone thinks you meant them.
senses.example: We are cognizant of the concentration risk, and the phased rollout is the answer to it.

cues.text: You are drafting a paper and want a formal way to record that the team already weighed the risk the committee is about to raise.
A regulator asks whether the implications were understood at the time, and they were.
Writing to a landlord about a repair, you want to acknowledge that he has other tenants without sounding casual about your own problem.
Explaining a decision to a family member, you want a slightly formal way of saying their situation was in view the whole way through.

distractors: Able to reason a problem through step by step, holding several moving parts in mind at once without losing the thread.
Formally notified of something in writing, so that a record exists showing the message was sent and received.

Sceptical of a claim until somebody puts hard evidence in front of you, and willing to keep saying so while the rest of the room has already moved on. It reports a standing disposition towards proof rather than a state of having noticed anything in particular.

Considerate of how other people are feeling and adjusting what you say to fit it, so that a hard message lands without doing damage nobody needed. It is care aimed at the person in front of you rather than attention paid to a fact.

In agreement with a stated position, to the point of putting your name next to it in front of people who will hold you to it later. It reports where you finally landed on the question, not what you had in view while the question was being decided.
